title: Evergreen dispensary apparel capsule -- turn five hand-painted crest panels (mixed studio light, in-frame grey reference) into burnable screen-print separations: vector spot masters for the flat designs, a holdable one-ink halftone for the continuous-tone one, plus a per-panel separation sell-sheet for the decorator
one_line_ask: Neutralise five differently-lit hand-painted capsule panels to one common clean white using each panel's in-frame grey reference, then prepare each as press-ready separation art in whichever form it actually needs -- clean vector spot master, genuinely knocked-out and tone-merged single-screen master, or continuous-tone art reseparated into a one-ink halftone with the house distress texture -- recognise the one supplied file that is a product photo (not artwork) and route it to a webshop packshot instead of the tracer, vectorise the wordmark, and lay the finished separations up as a one-page-per-panel sell-sheet for the decorator.
grounding_note: ADAPTED from a real Upwork apparel-capsule brief: a vertically-integrated cannabis retailer (laundered to the fictional 'Evergreen', an invented dispensary brand -- a generic dictionary word, no real-trademark collision) wanted 'a production-ready apparel design system for a branded retail capsule' that 'hands cleanly to manufacturers and decorators (vectors, tech packs)', 'purple-and-black forward, premium and confident, with slight reference to pink in intentional places', in an 'elevated streetwear' direction, on-palette with no rework. From-scratch garment art creation and embroidery digitising are out of an image-connector's scope, so this is REPOSITIONED to the production work a screen-print shop actually does and the connector CAN do: the decorator has received the capsule's finished hand-painted crest panels and must turn each into art the exposure room can burn, honouring the brief's own 'vectors that hand cleanly to decorators' and 'premium, on-palette, no rework' bar. STRENGTHENED against the audit (this task was flagged G3 'repetition sold as difficulty' -- a single hero recipe padded with upload/finalize plumbing -- and G5 'wrong tool': the previous version selected 'the stray magenta/teal accents' with image_select_by_prompt, which cannot target a hue, then solid-filled them, and it ended on a passive .ai export that added no difficulty). The amputated single hero is restored to a genuine FIVE-panel batch scanned across two different studio light setups, each panel carrying an in-frame 18% grey reference and corner registration ticks, so cross-asset white-point consistency becomes a real gradeable target; the illegal hue-select-and-fill is replaced by a legal named-motif selection + masked desaturate-and-darken; and the endpoint is now an agent-owned authored page-layout per-panel separation sell-sheet merge (one page per panel, page-count = row-count), not a passive template export. IP laundering: the aesthetic-direction name-drops in the original brief (a well-known streetwear label and two boutique embroidery houses) are removed and replaced with the generic phrase 'the house's elevated-streetwear direction'; no craft-software product name is used in any task-facing field (page-layout template, vector artwork, colour grade -- never the app names). The specific brand inks (purple #4B2E83 / black #0B0B0B / accent pink #E8669E), the crest subjects, and the authored .indd sell-sheet template are invented stand-ins so the chain is executable; no deliverable outside the brief was introduced, and the 'worn premium hand-feel' the brand references is produced in-chain by a halftone + grain pass, not by a supplied stock texture.
full_brief:
Evergreen, a dispensary chain, is putting its Fall/Spring elevated-streetwear apparel capsule into production and needs the front and back prints handed to our screen-print shop as art the exposure room can actually burn. We are NOT redesigning anything -- the designer has already hand-painted the capsule's crest panels and we are preparing what we were given for the press.

We are sending you the panels as flatbed scans. Fair warning up front: they were painted and scanned across two different sessions on different days, so they do NOT match -- some are cooler and a little dim, others warmer and brighter, and each sits a little crooked on the bed. Every painted panel has a small 18% grey reference swatch and corner registration ticks in its bottom margin. Before you touch anything else, get each panel's paper reading as one clean, identical, neutral white by eye off that grey swatch, using whatever straighten angle and temperature/tint/exposure moves THAT panel needs -- if the panels are cleaned to different whites, the brand purples drift and the six garments won't read as one drop. Tell us, per panel, the straighten angle and the tone/white-balance moves you settled on, so we can trust they really are matched.

Our shop rules, and the bar each panel must hit -- part of the job is deciding, per panel, which situation you are looking at, because getting it wrong won't show until it's on a shirt: (1) our manual press holds a limited number of screens and every ink prints as its own solid screen, so a design built from flat spot colours must come back as clean crisp VECTOR separation art where each colour is a solid holdable shape, one solid screen per ink. (2) A background has to be GENUINELY transparent -- if a panel still carries a stray off-white paper matte or halo, that matte burns as a phantom screen and prints as a ghost box, so it must be truly knocked out before anything else, not just look clean on screen. (3) The brand palette is locked (deep purple #4B2E83, black #0B0B0B, and pink #E8669E in intentional places only); if a panel carries a stray hand-mixed accent that is off that palette, or secretly uses several near-identical tones of what is really ONE ink, those have to be brought back onto one holdable screen before tracing -- we are not burning extra screens to print what should be one. (4) Some art is not spot-separable at all: anything built from smooth painted washes, blends or soft bleeds is continuous tone, and a manual mesh cannot hold unlimited tones -- that art has to be reseparated into a single HALFTONE screen (one ink, dot pattern) the mesh can hold, and it is exactly the panel where we want the worn, premium distress texture the house's elevated-streetwear direction is known for, so give it a subtle grain pass. Do NOT leave a wash as a gradient and do NOT force-trace it into a tangle of vector paths that will never register.

One more thing: not everything in the folder is artwork. One file is a photo of a finished printed tee on fabric -- it's only there so you can see how the ink sits. It must NOT go anywhere near the tracer; give us a clean webshop cut-out of it instead. Also vectorise the plain wordmark bitmap into scalable line art for the decorator.

Deliverables: each panel's finished separation in the correct form; the wordmark line art; the tee packshot; and a laid-up SEPARATION SELL-SHEET -- one page per panel -- that drops each finished separation into our template alongside its garment placement, print size and ink-limit note from the production roster we're sending, exported press-ready so the exposure room and the client both have one clean reference. Bind the roster copy verbatim -- don't rewrite our placements or sizes. Keep everything spot / halftone oriented for screen print -- no process-colour conversion, no new artwork, no recolouring a design to a different palette.

inputs.name: capsule_frontcrest_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A high-resolution flatbed-scanner capture of a hand-painted apparel graphic on cream textured watercolour paper: a symmetrical mountain-peak crest with a stylised lotus and small sun motif, painted in exactly two flat spot inks -- a deep purple (#4B2E83) and a near-black (#0B0B0B) -- with hard clean shape edges and no gradients. In the bottom margin print a small neutral 18% grey reference swatch and four black corner registration ticks. The capture is slightly COOL and a touch dim (mild blue-grey cast, cream paper reading dull not bright), lit a little unevenly, with visible paper fibre and brush texture inside the shapes, and the whole sheet sits about +2.7 degrees clockwise off level with uneven cream margins. Documentary art-scan realism, real paper fibre, no CGI gloss. About 4500 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: PANEL A -- the clean flat 2-spot control, cool session. Correct treatment: straighten the ~+2.7deg tilt, neutralise the cool cast BY EYE off the in-frame grey swatch (the agent never reads a channel/hex value -- it dials temperature/tint/exposure until the swatch LOOKS neutral and the paper reads a clean white, and reports what it dialled), crop to bounds DROPPING the grey swatch and ticks, then whole-raster vectorize into a 2-colour spot master. Nothing to knock out, nothing to merge. Deliberately shot COOL and tilted differently from the warm-session panels so a single blind cleanup recipe applied to the whole batch fails: this panel and Panel E share the cool session; Panels B/C/D are warm -- all must converge on ONE white point by eye. Declared ~4500 px so every raster output downscales, never upscales. Same file KIND (a raw .png scan) as every other panel so nothing telegraphs which treatment it needs.

inputs.name: capsule_backbanner_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A high-resolution flatbed scan of a hand-painted apparel back-print on cream textured paper: a horizontal banner crest reading a short brand tagline inside a ribbon, with a compass-rose motif, painted in three flat spot inks -- deep purple (#4B2E83), near-black (#0B0B0B) and accent pink (#E8669E) -- hard clean edges, no gradients. The painter's corner registration/crop ticks and the standard 18% grey reference swatch sit together in the bottom margin. Cool session look (mild blue-grey cast, dull paper), sheet rotated about +1.9 degrees clockwise, generous cream margin. Documentary scan realism, real paper fibre, about 4500 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: PANEL B -- clean flat 3-spot, cool session. Distinct from Panel A in that it carries THREE flat brand inks (it adds the accent pink as its own solid screen) where Panel A carries two, so the trace must return a clean 3-colour spot master with each ink a solid holdable shape and the pink correctly separated as its own screen rather than merged into the purple. Correct treatment: straighten, neutralise by eye off the grey swatch (report the dialled settings), then crop TIGHT to the artwork bounds -- dropping the bottom-margin grey swatch AND the corner registration/crop ticks and all surplus cream paper together (they are margin marks, not artwork; like every other painted panel the trace sees only the crest on clean ground) -- then whole-raster vectorize into a 3-colour spot master. The trap here is cropping so loose the grey swatch gets traced into the art, or mis-reading the three-ink art as fewer screens and collapsing the pink into the purple. Cool session, so its by-eye moves resemble Panel A's but its own tilt/exposure differ. ~4500 px.

inputs.name: capsule_leftchest_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A high-resolution flatbed scan of a small hand-painted left-chest emblem on cream textured paper: a compact leaf-and-crescent crest painted mostly in deep purple (#4B2E83) and near-black (#0B0B0B), BUT with a few hand-mixed teal leaf-sprig accents at the base that are clearly OFF the brand palette. Around the whole emblem sits a faint off-white 1-2 px halo / leftover matte from a sloppy scan export, so the background is NOT cleanly transparent. Hard flat shapes otherwise, the 18% grey reference swatch and corner ticks in the bottom margin. WARM session look (mild amber cast, paper reading slightly hot/bright), sheet rotated about -3.4 degrees counter-clockwise. Documentary scan realism, real paper fibre, about 4500 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: PANEL C -- the knock-out-AND-bring-onto-palette case, warm session. Three real problems: (1) a stray off-white halo/matte that must be GENUINELY removed to transparency with image_remove_background BEFORE tracing, else it burns as a phantom screen; (2) a small cluster of off-brand teal leaf-sprig accents that must be pulled back onto the locked palette -- and because the connector CANNOT select 'the teal region' by hue, the agent must select the accents as a NAMED MOTIF ('the small painted leaf-sprig accents at the base of the crest') with image_select_by_prompt, then on that mask DESATURATE and DARKEN them into the near-black brand ink with a masked image_apply_adjustments (a legal desaturate-and-darken move -- not a >90deg hue rotation to a target hex, which the connector cannot do); (3) the usual straighten + by-eye neutralisation to the common white point. Correct chain: straighten -> neutralise -> remove_background -> named-select the accents -> masked desaturate/darken -> crop to bounds (drop the swatch) -> whole-raster vectorize. The trap: tracing the raw file bakes in the halo rectangle and leaves the off-brand teal as a stray extra screen. Warm session -- opposite-direction white-balance to Panels A/E.

inputs.name: capsule_sleeve_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A high-resolution flatbed scan of a slim hand-painted sleeve mark on cream textured paper: a vertical stacked-word mark with a thin bordered rule, painted in what LOOKS like one dark ink but is actually a near-duplicate trio of very dark tones -- a soft charcoal, a warm near-black, and a true black -- that a novice would read as a single colour. Hard flat shapes, the 18% grey reference swatch and corner ticks in the bottom margin, on cream paper. WARM session look (amber cast, bright paper), sheet rotated about -2.2 degrees counter-clockwise. Documentary scan realism, real paper fibre, about 4500 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: PANEL D -- the hidden-multi-tone-ink case, warm session. The mark is really ONE screen but was painted in three near-duplicate darks; if traced as-is it splits one ink across three screens the manual press should not be burning. Correct chain: straighten -> neutralise by eye off the grey swatch (warm session moves) -> remove_background (knock the paper ground to transparency) -> image_select_by_prompt on 'the dark stacked-word linework and border rule' (a named shape, not a hue) -> masked image_apply_adjustments dropping saturation to zero and pushing blacks/contrast so the three near-dupe darks COLLAPSE to one flat ink -> crop to bounds (drop the swatch) -> whole-raster vectorize into a single-ink master. Distinct from Panel C: C is a chromatic off-brand accent collapsed onto palette; D is an achromatic near-dupe-tone merge to one screen. The trap is tracing raw and shipping a 3-screen mark. ~4500 px.

inputs.name: capsule_fullback_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A high-resolution flatbed scan of a large hand-painted full-back graphic on cream textured paper: a mountain-range-at-dusk scene painted as a SMOOTH continuous-tone watercolour wash -- a graded purple-to-deep-plum sky bleeding softly into a solid dark ridgeline, with soft feathered edges and no hard colour breaks -- clearly painterly continuous tone, not flat spot art. The 18% grey reference swatch and corner ticks in the bottom margin, cream paper. COOL session look (mild blue-grey cast, dull paper), sheet rotated about +3.1 degrees clockwise. Documentary art-scan realism, visible paper fibre and brush bleed, about 4500 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: PANEL E -- the continuous-tone case, cool session; the one that is NOT spot-separable and the one the brief wants the worn distress texture on. A graded wash plus soft bleed is effectively unlimited tones a manual mesh cannot hold, and force-tracing it to vector yields an unusable tangle of paths. Correct treatment: straighten -> neutralise by eye off the grey swatch (cool session, matched white point to Panel A) -> crop to bounds (drop the swatch) -> DESATURATE to a clean single-ink tonal ramp FIRST (masked/global image_apply_adjustments: drop saturation to zero, set contrast/whites/blacks so the ridgeline stays solid and the sky maps to a printable tonal range) -> image_apply_halftone so the continuous tone becomes a dot screen ONE ink can print -> image_add_grain for the worn premium distress hand-feel the house direction is known for. Halftoning the still-COLOUR wash directly gives colour moire garbage: the desaturate-first step is the intermediate the halftone depends on. Cool session. ~4500 px so the halftone downscales to press size, never up.

inputs.name: capsule_teeshot_photo.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal flat-lay product photo of a finished printed heavyweight tee laid on a smooth light-grey studio sweep, shot slightly from above. A deep-purple mountain crest with a pink accent is screen-printed on the chest, sitting on real woven cotton fabric with visible knit texture, soft folds, wrinkles and specular sheen catching the light. The tee is the clear main subject, centred, with a soft contact shadow on the sweep. Documentary catalog realism, real fabric, no CGI gloss. About 4000 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE DECOY. It looks like 'another panel of the crest' but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of a print on folded, textured fabric -- it CANNOT be traced into clean vector (fabric weave, folds, perspective and sheen would become garbage paths) and it has no grey reference swatch because it is not a paint panel. Its only correct use is the webshop packshot: knock the studio sweep to transparency with image_remove_background, then downscale/reframe to the product tile (a pure downscale from the ~4000 px source -- never upscale/canvas-extend). A naive agent that runs it through the same straighten/neutralise/vectorize path it used on the paint panels produces an unusable trace; the failure is only visible in the path data. Same file KIND concern: it is a raster image in the same folder, so the agent must DECIDE it is a photo, not artwork -- nothing in a client field labels it.

inputs.name: evergreen_wordmark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat bitmap PNG of the wordmark 'Evergreen' set in a confident high-contrast condensed serif, solid deep-purple (#4B2E83) letterforms on a plain white background, clean even kerning, centred, no effects or gradients -- a logo handoff bitmap as a client would email it. Crisp but rasterised (slightly soft pixel edges, not vector). About 3000 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: Text-bearing asset -> gemini-3-pro-image for accurate legible lettering. Deliberately a flat raster (not already vector) so the whole-raster vectorize step into scalable line art is justified. Solid single-ink purple wordmark on white, so the trace is a clean single-colour line-art master; no knockout or tone-merge needed.

inputs.name: evergreen_sepsheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client/studio-supplied, not model-generated): a genuine hand-built page-layout SINGLE-RECORD separation sell-sheet template (.indd/.idml, ~US Letter portrait at 300 DPI plus bleed) -- ONE panel per page. It carries live data-merge placeholder fields <<design_name>>, <<garment_placement>>, <<print_size>>, <<ink_limit_note>>, a masthead area, and ONE image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path merge column so the merge drops each finished separation preview into the sheet. Built by hand so the merge fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a PDF-converted template and NOT a multi-record grid: the merge emits one file per row.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd with real <<fields>> PLUS a genuine @-image-path column, and produces ONE PAGE PER ROW -- five roster rows => five single-record sheets. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted template or a multi-record grid would not bind / cannot be produced by this tool. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool here (text-only, cannot bind the @-image column).

inputs.name: evergreen_production_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns design_name,garment_placement,print_size,ink_limit_note,@sep_preview holding exactly five rows, one per painted panel: 'Front Crest' (front-centre-chest, 11 in wide, 'manual press, max 4 screens'); 'Back Banner' (upper-back, 12 in wide, 'manual press, max 4 screens'); 'Left-Chest Emblem' (front-left-chest, 4 in wide, 'manual press, max 3 screens'); 'Sleeve Mark' (left-sleeve, 2.5 in wide, 'manual press, max 2 screens'); 'Full-Back Graphic' (full-back, 13 in wide, 'manual press, single halftone screen'). The @sep_preview column names the matching finished-separation preview PNG the agent produces (e.g. @frontcrest_preview.png). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the @-image column.
inputs.realism_notes: Neutral production metadata only -- garment placement, print size, ink-limit note. It deliberately does NOT hand the solver the separation treatment: the design_name is a placement label, not a diagnosis, and the @sep_preview column binds a raster PREVIEW (PNG) for EVERY row regardless of whether that panel's master is an SVG spot trace or a PNG halftone, so no file extension or 'type' column telegraphs which panel needs which treatment. Which panel is flat-spot vs knockout-and-merge vs continuous-tone-halftone is the agent's decision. Five rows => the one-page-per-row merge must produce exactly five sheets. Ink-limit hints ('single halftone screen' on the full-back) describe the shop's press constraint, not the tool path.

outputs.name: frontcrest_sep.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector spot-separation master of the front crest: the two flat brand inks preserved as solid holdable shapes with crisp edges, traced from the straightened, grey-neutralised, cropped-to-bounds art (grey reference swatch cropped out). A genuine 2-screen spot master, not a silhouette and not a raster. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: backbanner_sep.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector spot-separation master of the back banner: three flat brand inks preserved as solid holdable shapes with crisp edges (the accent pink separated as its own screen), traced from the straightened, grey-neutralised, cropped-to-bounds art; the grey reference swatch and the bottom-margin registration/crop ticks cropped out together. A genuine 3-screen spot master, not a silhouette and not a raster. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: leftchest_sep.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector spot-separation master of the left-chest emblem: the stray off-white halo GENUINELY knocked out to transparency (no phantom-screen matte) and the off-brand teal accents desaturated-and-darkened back onto the locked palette before tracing, so the result is an on-palette master with no captured paper ground and no stray extra screen. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: sleeve_sep.svg
outputs.spec: Clean single-ink vector spot-separation master of the sleeve mark: the three near-duplicate dark tones collapsed to ONE flat ink before tracing, the paper ground knocked out, so the mark is one holdable screen, not three. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: fullback_halftone_distress.png
outputs.spec: A single-ink HALFTONE separation of the continuous-tone full-back graphic: the graded wash and soft bleed first reduced to a clean one-ink tonal ramp (ridgeline held solid), then converted to a visible halftone dot screen the manual mesh can hold, then given a subtle grain/distress pass for the worn premium hand-feel -- a burnable one-screen separation, NOT a continuous-tone gradient and NOT a force-traced vector tangle. Downscaled to press size from the ~4500 px source (never upscaled). A single-ink dot-screen separation at print resolution -- no image_remove_background step is used (after crop-to-bounds the panel is edge-to-edge painted scene with no outer paper ground to isolate; the light areas simply carry no dots and burn open on the mesh). DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: wordmark_vector.svg
outputs.spec: Vectorised Evergreen wordmark: scalable solid-purple single-ink line art for print/embroidery handoff, traced from the supplied flat bitmap. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: capsule_packshot_web.jpg
outputs.spec: Webshop product cut-out of the printed-tee photo: the studio sweep knocked out by image_remove_background and the subject reframed/downscaled to a product tile (1600x2000, sRGB, on white). A RASTER packshot with no vector paths -- this file proves the tee photo was correctly triaged as a photograph, not routed to the tracer. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: Evergreen_Capsule_SepSheets.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly five press-ready US Letter portrait separation sell-sheets -- ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 5) -- exported from the one-page-per-row data-merge; each sheet drops that panel's finished separation preview into the image frame and binds <<design_name>>/<<garment_placement>>/<<print_size>>/<<ink_limit_note>> verbatim from the roster; ~300 DPI. The agent-owned designed endpoint. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: Evergreen_Capsule_PrintPackage.zip
outputs.spec: Single decorator handoff bundle containing the four vector spot masters, the halftone-distress PNG, the wordmark vector, the tee packshot, the retained card-bearing neutralised reference masters, and the five-page separation sell-sheet PDF. DELIVERABLE.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: capsule_frontcrest_scan.png, capsule_backbanner_scan.png, capsule_leftchest_scan.png, capsule_sleeve_scan.png, capsule_fullback_scan.png, capsule_teeshot_photo.jpg, evergreen_wordmark.png, evergreen_sepsheet_template.indd, evergreen_production_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Single batch ingest: bring the five painted panel scans, the tee photo, the wordmark bitmap, the authored single-record sell-sheet template and the production roster into the working project so every downstream step has real asset references. This is the only raw asset load -- plumbing, not the difficulty; every later step consumes a named prior output.
Level the front-crest scan so the crest sits square before cropping and tracing. Report the correcting angle you used on this panel -- it is not the same as the other panels' angles.

Neutralise this panel BY EYE: dial temperature/tint/exposure until the in-frame 18% grey reference swatch looks neutral and the paper reads a clean white, judged visually -- never read a pixel, channel or hex value. Report the settings you dialled. These moves are specific to this panel's light; do not reuse another panel's settings. This neutralised scan (swatch still in frame) is the retained card-bearing reference master for this panel.
Crop tight to the crest artwork, dropping the bottom-margin grey swatch, the registration ticks and all surplus cream paper so the trace sees only the artwork on clean ground. Report the crop bounds.

Trace the prepared front crest into a clean vector spot master -- each ink a solid holdable shape, edges crisp. Feeding a prepared raster (not a selection) so the trace returns a colour separation, not a black silhouette. DELIVERABLE frontcrest_sep.svg.

Downscale the prepared front-crest raster to the sell-sheet preview size (the @sep_preview cell the merge binds for the Front Crest row). Downscale-only from the ~4500 px source, never canvas-extend, never upscale.
Level the back-banner scan. Report this panel's correcting angle.

Neutralise this panel by eye off its grey swatch to the SAME clean white as the other panels, using its own temperature/tint/exposure moves; report them. Retained card-bearing reference master for this panel.

Crop tight to the banner artwork, dropping the bottom-margin grey swatch, the corner registration/crop ticks and all surplus cream paper together so the trace sees only the artwork on clean ground. Report the crop bounds.

Trace the prepared back banner into a clean vector spot master keeping the three flat inks as solid holdable shapes with the accent pink separated as its own screen. Prepared raster in (not a selection). DELIVERABLE backbanner_sep.svg.
Downscale the prepared back-banner raster to the sell-sheet preview size for the Back Banner row. Downscale-only from source.
Level the left-chest emblem scan. Report this panel's correcting angle.

Neutralise this panel by eye off its grey swatch to the common clean white; its cast runs opposite to the cool-session panels so its moves differ in sign. Report them. Retained card-bearing reference master.

Bring this panel to a genuinely transparent ground before any tracing, so no residual paper matte or halo survives to burn as a phantom screen. This is the knockout-to-transparency path, NOT select->invert->fill (which would solid-fill and destroy interior gaps).

Select the small painted leaf-sprig accent motifs at the base of the crest as a NAMED shape (a real object/part, not a colour or region) to confine the next move to those accents only. Returns a mask.

On the accent mask only, drop saturation to zero and darken so the off-brand accents collapse into the near-black brand ink, bringing the emblem fully onto the locked palette. A masked desaturate-and-darken (image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask); a bounded, in-range tonal move, not a hue rotation to a target hex. Report that you brought the accents onto palette.
Crop the now-transparent, on-palette emblem tight to its bounds, dropping the grey swatch and surplus ground so the trace sees only clean artwork. Report the crop bounds.

Trace the prepared emblem into a clean on-palette vector spot master -- no captured off-white rectangle (halo gone), no stray off-brand screen (accents collapsed). Prepared raster in. DELIVERABLE leftchest_sep.svg.
Downscale the prepared emblem raster to the sell-sheet preview size for the Left-Chest Emblem row. Downscale-only from source.
Level the sleeve-mark scan. Report this panel's correcting angle.
Neutralise this panel by eye off its grey swatch to the common clean white with its own moves; report them. Retained card-bearing reference master.
Knock the paper ground to transparency so the mark isolates cleanly before any tone work. Knockout-to-transparency path, not select->invert->fill.
Select the dark stacked-word linework and border rule as a NAMED shape (not a hue) so the tone-merge is confined to the mark's ink.

On the linework mask only, drop saturation to zero and push blacks/contrast so the near-duplicate dark tones collapse to ONE flat holdable ink -- reducing a hidden multi-screen mark to a single screen. Masked image_apply_adjustments; report that you merged the mark to one ink.
Crop the now-transparent, single-ink mark tight to its bounds, dropping the grey swatch. Report the crop bounds.
Trace the prepared mark into a clean single-ink vector master -- one screen, no captured ground. Prepared raster in. DELIVERABLE sleeve_sep.svg.
Downscale the prepared mark raster to the sell-sheet preview size for the Sleeve Mark row. Downscale-only from source.
Level the full-back graphic scan. Report this panel's correcting angle.
Neutralise this panel by eye off its grey swatch to the SAME clean white as the other cool-session panel; report the moves. Retained card-bearing reference master.
Crop tight to the painted scene, dropping the grey swatch and surplus paper. Report the crop bounds.

Reduce this panel to a clean single-ink tonal ramp: drop saturation to zero and set contrast/whites/blacks so the ridgeline stays solid and the graded sky maps to a printable tonal range. This desaturate-first step is the intermediate the next step depends on -- screening the still-colour wash directly would give colour moire. Report the tonal moves.

Convert the single-ink tonal ramp into a halftone dot screen so the continuous tone becomes variable-size dots a manual mesh can actually hold -- the whole graphic prints as ONE ink screen. This is the reseparation the continuous-tone art requires (no LPI parameter; apply and report that it was reseparated to a one-ink halftone).

Add a subtle grain/distress pass for the worn, premium hand-feel the house's elevated-streetwear direction is known for -- produced in-chain, replacing any supplied stock paper texture. DELIVERABLE fullback_halftone_distress.png.
Downscale the finished halftone-distress separation to the sell-sheet preview size for the Full-Back Graphic row. Downscale-only from the ~4500 px source, never upscale.

difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon create-edit rebuilt from the audit's G3 (repetition) and G5 (wrong-tool) flags: 44 connector calls, 16 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* prep/select/adjust/halftone/grain/vectorize, document_* merge/export, asset_* storage), well past the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single ingest and the two merge-upload plumbing steps. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth: the five painted panels are superficially the same kind of file (raw crest scans) but need FIVE divergent correct treatments, and each treatment is a dependent chain where a wrong intermediate breaks the downstream op -- knocking out the halo is a prerequisite for a clean trace; collapsing the near-dupe darks to one ink is a prerequisite for a one-screen master; desaturating the wash to one ink is a prerequisite for a clean halftone (screening the colour wash gives moire). Layered on top is a genuine cross-asset consistency target: the panels were scanned across two light sessions (cool: Front Crest, Back Banner, Full-Back; warm: Left-Chest, Sleeve), each with an in-frame 18% grey reference, and all must be neutralised BY EYE to one common white point with divergent per-panel moves -- a single blind recipe drifts the brand purples and the capsule stops reading as one drop. The previous version's illegal hue-select-and-fill is replaced by a legal named-motif selection + masked desaturate-and-darken (Left-Chest accents, Sleeve near-dupe darks), which respects that selection is semantic and that the connector cannot do a >90deg hue rotation. It respects every connector limit: image_vectorize is fed prepared rasters (not selections) so it returns real colour separations; image_remove_background yields transparency, not a composite, and is never asked to punch an enclosed hole; image_crop_and_resize / image_crop_to_bounds only downscale/trim from ~4500 px (~4000 px for the photo) declared sources, never upscale or canvas-extend; image_apply_halftone reseparates a desaturated ramp (no LPI claim); the endpoint is a genuine authored-.indd one-page-per-row data merge (five rows -> five sheets, @-image column binding each finished preview, page=row and ~300 DPI acceptance), not a passive template export; convert_pdf_to_indd and document_merge_data_vector are avoided; deprecated adjust tools are replaced by image_apply_adjustments. The agent performs NO measurement -- it neutralises by eye and reports the parameters it applied.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, never a self-measurement): the five painted panels look like the same kind of scan but need five divergent separation treatments, and the agent trips the gate by mis-triaging -- vectorising the continuous-tone full-back wash (an unusable tangle of paths) or halftoning it while it is still colour (moire garbage); tracing the left-chest emblem before its phantom paper halo is knocked out (a captured off-white rectangle that burns as a ghost screen) or leaving its off-brand teal accents as a stray extra screen; tracing the sleeve mark's three near-duplicate darks as-is (three screens where the shop should burn one); or mis-reading the back banner's three flat inks and collapsing its accent pink into the purple so the trace returns too few screens. A second failure mode is running the tee PHOTO through the paint-panel path -- it looks like another crest but is a print on folded fabric and must go to remove_background for the packshot, not the tracer, or the SVG fills with garbage weave/fold paths. Every one of these is invisible on screen and only shows on the press, so the grader checks the delivered files. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset white-point consistency across two deliberately mismatched light sessions -- the agent must dial DIFFERENT straighten angles and OPPOSITE-direction white-balance moves that all land each panel's in-frame grey reference neutral and drive the batch to one clean shared white, judged by eye and REPORTED as the parameters applied so 'matched' is checkable; (2) constraint-reasoning around tool limits -- a phantom matte removed via remove_background to transparency (not select->invert->fill); an off-brand accent brought onto palette via a NAMED-motif selection + masked desaturate-and-darken (because selection cannot target a hue and the connector cannot rotate a hue >90deg to a target hex); a hidden multi-tone ink collapsed to one screen via a masked adjustment before tracing; a continuous-tone wash held only as a one-ink halftone (not vector, not left continuous); (3) prep-before-trace discipline (straighten, neutralise, knock out, tone-merge, crop-to-bounds) so image_vectorize only ever sees clean prepared artwork. TRAP: the naive uniform path -- straighten/neutralise/vectorize all five painted panels the same way because 'they're all crest scans' -- looks right and fails on the wash (tangle), the emblem (baked halo + stray screen), the sleeve (three screens) and, worse, on the tee photo (weave garbage); a second trap halftones the colour wash directly instead of desaturating to one ink first. The AGENT-AUTHORED LOOK is the full-back reseparation: a reasoned desaturate-to-one-ink-ramp -> halftone -> grain sequence the agent must build from primitives (not a preset, not auto-tone) to turn an unprintable wash into a burnable, distressed one-ink screen. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, no agent pixel-reading): grade neutrality on the FIVE retained card-bearing neutralised reference masters (grey reference resolving to a common neutral white point across all five, no residual cast, no clipped white/crushed black -- the grey swatch is present ONLY on these retained masters; the delivered separations crop it out, checked separately for card-exclusion); the front-crest SVG a clean 2-ink spot master and the back-banner SVG a clean 3-ink master with the accent pink separated as its own screen; the left-chest SVG on-palette with no captured halo ground and no stray off-brand screen; the sleeve SVG a single-ink master; the full-back delivered as a visible one-ink halftone dot screen with grain (not a gradient, not a vector tangle) downscaled from source; capsule_packshot_web.jpg a raster at exactly 1600x2000 sRGB containing no vector paths; the merged sell-sheet page-count == roster row-count == 5 with each finished preview placed and its copy bound verbatim at ~300 DPI; every raster output reachable by downscale from the declared camera-scale sources. The agent reports its per-panel straighten angle and temperature/tint/exposure moves and the treatment it chose per panel -- an applied-settings/decision log, never a measured or recovered value.
